raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Yeah, hi. My name's Sarah. We got matched up here, right?
ParticipantB: Oh, hi Sarah. I'm Mike. Yeah, that's what they said. You in Chicago too?
ParticipantA: Yeah, moved out here three years ago. Working as an electrician now.
ParticipantB: Oh, nice. I drive a school bus. Out in the north suburbs.
ParticipantA: Wow, okay. That's different. I mean, wiring houses is good, but driving kids? Seems... weird to me.
ParticipantB: Haha, yeah, it is a bit. My son is on my bus. He's in third grade.
ParticipantA: Really? Your kid rides with you? That's a lot of responsibility.
ParticipantB: It is. But honestly, I'm pretty skeptical about the whole electrician thing.
ParticipantA: Why's that? I love it. People always ask me, "Why did you pick this?" I just knew it since I was twelve. Can't really explain why, but I just liked being with wires.
ParticipantB: Oh, I see. Well, my brother-in-law is one. He's a real pro. But he never talks about it like you do. Seems like he just does it for the money, you know?
ParticipantA: Hmm. Maybe. But I feel like it's the only thing that makes sense to me. I can't imagine doing anything else.
ParticipantB: Yeah, maybe. My son keeps saying, "Dad, why don't you fix his house?" He wants me to go into trades. But I don't get that same feeling.
ParticipantA: That's interesting. My little sister is 14, she wants to be an electrician. She's like, "It's so cool, Sarah!" But I just tell her to wait, she's too young.
ParticipantB: Yeah, that's smart. She's not ready. My kid's just a kid, but he thinks driving is boring now that he's older.
ParticipantA: Oh, really? That's tough. I think I'd enjoy teaching a kid that stuff. Do you ever try to teach him?
ParticipantB: Not really. I just tell him to get good grades. He wants to be a lawyer or something. I don't think he'll be interested in wires.
ParticipantA: Maybe. But you never know. My nephew is 8, he wanted to be an electrician last week. Said he liked the sparks.
ParticipantB: (Laughs) Sparks? Yeah, I guess that sounds dangerous. I worry about him more than I do about the work itself.
ParticipantA: True. Safety is huge with kids. I never worry about my girls doing electrical work. They're too scared of it.
ParticipantB: Yeah, that's good. I think that's why I stay in driving. It's safer. But sometimes I feel like I'm missing out on something.
ParticipantA: Maybe. But I'm happy with it. I fix a house every day, and it feels real.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I guess. Well, I gotta go, the kids are getting on the bus.
ParticipantA: Oh, okay. Good talking to you, Mike.
ParticipantB: You too, Sarah. Have a good one.
ParticipantA: Bye.
